analyst.summary: Adani Ports had a strong FY26 operationally - a record 500.8 million tonnes of cargo, 25% revenue growth, and a rare sovereign-matching credit rating upgrade from S&P - but profit growth (15.6%) lagged revenue growth because interest costs more than doubled as debt from its Australian coal-terminal purchase and Kerala transshipment-port expansion came onto the books, and margins eased in the March quarter. The stock trades at roughly 33 times trailing earnings, above its own long-run average, at a time when the company's own guidance for the coming year points to materially slower growth than it has delivered recently. The underlying port and logistics business remains genuinely well run and well capitalised, but a rich valuation, a fresh related-party-transaction pattern similar to one that cost the company its auditor in 2023, and an unresolved US legal case against the promoters argue for holding rather than adding at current levels.
